extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners (primary); patent practitioners and applicants
extracted.subtask_description: Form-paragraph guidance from the MPEP for examiners on handling benefit claims, continuity/CPA issues, inventorship corrections, foreign priority, reexamination/SNQ determinations, and international design reproductions. Specifies which form paragraphs to use and the substantive/legal criteria that trigger them.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 2.01 Possible Status as Divisional
rubrics_metrics.description: This application discloses and claims only subject matter disclosed in prior Application No. [1], filed [2], appears to claim only subject matter directed to an invention independent and distinct from that claimed in the prior application, and names the inventor or at least one joint inventor named in the prior application; accordingly it may constitute a divisional application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Should applicant desire to claim benefit of the prior filing date, direct attention to 35 U.S.C. 120, 37 CFR 1.78, and MPEP § 211 et seq. Examiner notes: insert prior application number and filing date in brackets; use only if application may be a divisional but no proper benefit claim established; do not call a 35 U.S.C. 119(e) provisional-derived application a 'continuation' of the prior application.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 2.05 Possible Status as Continuation
rubrics_metrics.description: This application discloses and claims only subject matter disclosed in prior Application No. [1], filed [2], and names the inventor or at least one joint inventor named in the prior application; accordingly, this application may constitute a continuation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant desires to claim the benefit of the prior filing date, direct attention to 35 U.S.C. 120, 37 CFR 1.78, and MPEP § 211 et seq. Examiner notes: insert prior application number and filing date; use only if it appears application may be a continuation but no benefit claim properly established; do not call an application claiming a 35 U.S.C. 119(e) provisional a 'continuation' of the prior application.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 2.06 Possible Status as Continuation-in-Part
rubrics_metrics.description: This application repeats a substantial portion of prior Application No. [1], filed [2], and adds additional disclosure not presented in the prior application; because it names the inventor or at least one joint inventor named in the prior application, it may constitute a continuation-in-part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant desires to claim the benefit of the prior filing date, direct attention to 35 U.S.C. 120, 37 CFR 1.78, and MPEP § 211 et seq. Examiner notes: insert prior application number and filing date; use only if application may qualify as a CIP but no benefit claim properly established; do not call an application claiming a 119(e) provisional a 'continuation-in-part' of the prior application.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 2.03 Affidavits or Declarations in Prior Application
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavits or declarations filed during prosecution of a prior application do not automatically become part of this application; to rely on an earlier affidavit/declaration the applicant should make the remarks of record in this application and include a copy of the original affidavit or declaration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use only in applications filed under 37 CFR 1.53(b). Do not use in 37 CFR 1.53(d) filings because affidavits/declarations submitted during prosecution of a parent nonprovisional automatically become part of a 1.53(d) application.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 2.07 Definition of a Substitute
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'substitute' application is essentially a duplicate of an application abandoned before filing of the later application; a 'substitute' does not obtain the benefit of the filing date of the prior application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to explain that calling an application a 'substitute' is not a basis for benefit claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 2.09 Heading for Conditions for Benefit Claims Under 35 U.S.C. 119(e), 120, 121, 365(c), or 386(c)
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledges applicant's claim for benefit of a prior-filed application but that applicant has not complied with one or more conditions for receiving the benefit under the identified statutory sections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert appropriate statutory section(s) in bracket. One or more of form paragraphs 2.10–2.11.01 or 2.38–2.40 must follow depending on circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 2.10 Disclosure of Prior-Filed Application Does Not Provide Support for Claimed Subject Matter
rubrics_metrics.description: The disclosure of the prior-filed application fails to provide adequate support or enablement under 35 U.S.C. 112(a) (or pre-AIA 112) for one or more claims of this application; therefore those claims are not entitled to the benefit of the prior filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be preceded by heading form paragraph 2.09. Can be used when lack of support/enablement in prior-filed application for claims in the later-filed application claiming benefit under 35 U.S.C. 120, 121, 365(c), 386(c) or 119(e). In bracket 1 insert prior application number; in bracket 2 provide explanation and list of claims not entitled to benefit if only some claims affected.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 2.10.01 Continuation or Divisional Application Contains New Matter Relative to the Prior-Filed Application
rubrics_metrics.description: A continuation or divisional application cannot include new matter; the application contains matter not disclosed in the prior-filed application and thus applicant must delete the benefit claim or change the relationship to continuation-in-part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when an application claiming benefit under 35 U.S.C. 120, 121, 365(c), or 386(c) contains new matter relative to the prior-filed application and purports to be a continuation/division/divisional. In bracket 1 provide example of the matter not disclosed in prior-filed application. Do not use for 119(e) provisional benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 2.11 Application Must Be Copending With Parent
rubrics_metrics.description: Copendency between the current application and the prior application is required for benefit claims under 35 U.S.C. 120, 121, 365(c), or 386(c); if the applications are not copending, the benefit claim is improper and must be deleted unless copendency can be established.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be preceded by heading form paragraph 2.09. Do not use this paragraph for 35 U.S.C. 119(e) provisional benefit claims. Insert prior application number in bracket 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 2.11.01 Application Must Be Filed Within 12 Months From the Provisional Application Unless Petition Granted
rubrics_metrics.description: To claim benefit of a provisional under 35 U.S.C. 119(e) the later application must be filed within twelve months of the provisional filing date, unless a petition to restore benefit under 37 CFR 1.78(b) or PCT Rule 26bis.3 has been granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when an application claims benefit of a provisional but was not filed within twelve months and no intermediate application exists and no petition was granted. Explains contents of a 37 CFR 1.78(b) petition: reference to provisional, petition fee (37 CFR 1.17(m)), and statement that delay was unintentional; address for petition provided. Must be preceded by heading 2.09 and insert prior provisional application number in bracket 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 2.13 Correction of Inventorship Under 37 CFR 1.48(a), Insufficient
rubrics_metrics.description: The request to correct inventorship under 37 CFR 1.48(a) is deficient for specified reasons; potential rejections under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(f) or (g) must be considered if request denied; grant/denial may affect ability to claim benefit under 35 U.S.C. 120.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use only for requests to correct inventors in nonprovisional applications; if request is to delete an inventor due to canceled/amended claims use 2.13.01. Primary examiner may not decide requests accompanied by a 1.183 petition — forward to Office of Petitions. Follow with one or more of 2.13a–2.13e as applicable. See MPEP § 602.08(b) for name change issues; note procedures changed for requests filed on/after Sept 16, 2012 (handled by OPAP).

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 2.13.01 Correction of Inventorship Under 37 CFR 1.48(b), Insufficient
rubrics_metrics.description: The request for deletion of an inventor under 37 CFR 1.48(b) is deficient because it lacks required elements (e.g., written consent of assignee) or other defects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when inventorship was previously correct but an inventor is being deleted because claims were amended/canceled. Follow with form paragraphs 2.13c and/or 2.13g as applicable. See note 1 of 2.13 regarding potential rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 2.13d Written Consent Missing (for Use Following FP 2.13 or 2.13.02, If Applicable)
rubrics_metrics.description: The request to delete an inventor under 37 CFR 1.48(b) is deficient because it lacks the written consent of any assignee of one of the originally named inventors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when inventorship was correct at filing and deletion is requested due to amendments/cancellations. Follow with 2.13c and/or 2.13g. See potential rejections under 2.13 note 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 2.13.02 Correction of Inventorship Under 37 CFR 1.48(c), Insufficient
rubrics_metrics.description: The request to correct inventorship under 37 CFR 1.48(c) requesting addition of an inventor(s) is deficient because required elements are missing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when inventorship was previously correct but now needs change due to subsequent addition of subject matter from specification to claims contributed by a party not originally named. Follow with any of 2.13b–2.13e or 2.13h. Consider notes 2 and 4–7 of 2.13.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 2.13a Statement of Facts Problem (for Use Following FP 2.13, If Applicable)
rubrics_metrics.description: The statement of facts by an inventor(s) to be added or deleted does not explicitly state that the inventorship error occurred without deceptive intent or cannot be so construed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when the required statement of facts is inadequate to show lack of deceptive intent.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 2.13b No New Oath or Declaration (for Use Following FP 2.13 or 2.13.02, If Applicable)
rubrics_metrics.description: An oath or declaration by each actual inventor listing the entire inventive entity has not been submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow 2.13 or 2.13.02 when new oath/declaration is required but missing.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 2.13c Required Fee Not Submitted (for Use Following FP 2.13, 2.13.01 or 2.13.02, If Applicable)
rubrics_metrics.description: The request to correct inventorship lacks the required fee under 37 CFR 1.17(i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when 1.17(i) fee is missing; follow the primary deficiency paragraph with this paragraph as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 2.13e 37 CFR 3.73(b) Submission (for Use Following FP 2.13 or 2.13.02, If Applicable)
rubrics_metrics.description: A 37 CFR 3.73(b) submission has not been received to support action by the assignee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when assignee action requires a 3.73(b) submission and it is missing.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 2.13f Hostile Inventor(s)/Inventorship Overlap (for Use Following FP 2.13, If Applicable)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where it appears a party required to submit a statement of facts may be unwilling (hostile) and inventorship would overlap original inventorship, applicant should consider petition under 37 CFR 1.183 to waive the requirement or refiling options under 37 CFR 1.53(b) or 1.53(d) to eliminate need for a 1.48 request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides alternative procedural remedies: petition under 1.183 if assignee consent exists; refiling under 1.53(b) with new oath/declaration and necessary petition; use appropriate methods to add/delete inventors. See MPEP § 602.01(c)(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 2.13g Statement Under 37 CFR 1.48(b)(2) Problem (for Use Following FP 2.13.01, If Applicable)
rubrics_metrics.description: The request was not accompanied by the statement required under 37 CFR 1.48(b)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow 2.13.01 when this specific statement is missing.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 2.13h Statement of Facts, Added Inventor (for Use Following FP 2.13.02, If Applicable)
rubrics_metrics.description: The statement of facts by the inventor(s) to be added does not explicitly state that the amendment of inventorship is necessitated by amendment of the claims and that the inventorship error occurred without deceptive intent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use after 2.13.02 when the added-inventor statement of facts fails to state required elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 2.14 Correction of Inventorship Under 37 CFR 1.48(a) or (c) Filed Before Sept. 16, 2012, Sufficient
rubrics_metrics.description: The request to correct inventorship filed before Sept. 16, 2012, is sufficient: inventorship has been changed in compliance with 37 CFR 1.48 and the application will be forwarded to OPAP for corrected filing receipt and Office records correction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert appropriate letter code a or c in bracket 1 and explain correction in bracket 2. Use only for requests filed before Sept. 16, 2012; requests filed on/after that date are handled by OPAP.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 2.14.01 Correction of Inventorship Under 37 CFR 1.48(b) Filed Before Sept. 16, 2012, Sufficient
rubrics_metrics.description: For 1.48(b) corrections filed before Sept. 16, 2012, the inventorship has been changed by deletion of [1] and the application forwarded to OPAP for corrected filing receipt and record correction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use only for 37 CFR 1.48(b) corrections filed before Sept. 16, 2012. In bracket 1 insert names of deleted inventor(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 2.15 Reference to Prior Application, 35 U.S.C. 119(e), 120, 121, 365(c), or 386(c) Benefit
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant desires to claim benefit of a prior-filed application under the cited statutes, the instant application must contain a specific reference to the prior-filed application in compliance with 37 CFR 1.78, located as required depending on filing date and application type; failure to timely submit specific reference results in waiver of benefit unless accompanied by a grantable petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details timing: for 35 U.S.C. 111(a) utility/plant apps: submit during pendency and within the later of 4 months from actual filing date or 16 months from prior filing date; for national stage under 371, timing differs as set forth. Requirement location changed for filings on/after Sept. 16, 2012 (ADS). Time period is not extendable but a petition under 37 CFR 1.78(c)/(e) may be accepted with required reference, petition fee (37 CFR 1.17(m)), and statement of unintentional delay. If reference was previously submitted but not in required location and recognized by Office (e.g., included on first filing receipt), petition/fee may not be required but applicant still must file ADS or amendment. Use when application references but does not claim benefit; insert prior app number/date in brackets and note CPA exception under 1.53(d). See MPEP § 211.02.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 2.18 Right of Priority Under 35 U.S.C. 119(a)-(d) and (f)
rubrics_metrics.description: Advises applicant of possible benefits under 35 U.S.C. 119(a)-(d) and (f) whereby a U.S. patent application may claim priority to a foreign application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General advisory; refer to MPEP sections on foreign priority and 37 CFR 1.55 for procedural requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 2.19 Overcome Rejection by Translation
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant cannot rely upon the certified copy of a foreign priority application to overcome a rejection because a translation of said application has not been made of record in accordance with 37 CFR 1.55.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this paragraph following a rejection based on an intervening reference. See MPEP §§ 215 and 216 and 37 CFR 1.55 requirements for translations.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 2.20 Certified Copies of Priority Papers in Parent or Related (Reissue Situation) - Application
rubrics_metrics.description: To obtain priority based on foreign priority papers filed in a parent or related application, a claim for such foreign priority must be timely made in this application and certified copies must satisfy 37 CFR 1.55; applicant may identify the parent nonprovisional application or patent containing the certified copy to satisfy 1.55.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when priority papers are in a parent/reissue situation; explains interplay with reissue and related applications and requirement of timely claim for priority.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 2.21.01 35 U.S.C. 119(a)-(d) or (f), 365(a) or (b), or 386(a) Foreign Priority Claim is Untimely
rubrics_metrics.description: A foreign priority claim filed on [1] was not entered because it was not filed within the time period set forth in 37 CFR 1.55; for original applications under 111(a) present within later of 4 months from actual filing date or 16 months from foreign filing date (and ADS requirement if filed on/after Sept.16,2012). Applicant must file a petition for an unintentionally delayed priority claim under 37 CFR 1.55(e) with specified contents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraph lists petition requirements: priority claim in accordance with 1.55, certified copy unless previously submitted or exception applies, petition fee (1.17(m)), and statement that the entire delay was unintentional; Director may require additional information. Use only for original 111(a) apps filed on/after Nov.29,2000 and national stage apps under 371; do not use for design applications. Insert date amendment/paper containing priority claim was filed in bracket 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 2.22 Certified Copy Filed, But Proper Claim Not Made
rubrics_metrics.description: Receipt is acknowledged of a certified copy of foreign application [1]; however, the present application does not properly claim priority to the submitted foreign application. To obtain priority applicant must also file a claim as required by 35 U.S.C. 119(b)/365(b) and 37 CFR 1.55 located in oath/declaration or ADS depending on filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains timing limits (later of 4 months or 16 months) and that a claim not presented within 1.55 is considered waived, though a petition under 1.55(e) for unintentional delay may be accepted. Use only for original 111(a) apps on/after Nov.29,2000 and national stage apps under 371; do not use for design applications. Insert foreign application number in bracket 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 2.25 Claimed Foreign Priority, No Papers Certified Copy Filed
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledgement of applicant's claim for foreign priority based on an application filed in [1] on [2], but applicant has not filed a certified copy of the application as required by 37 CFR 1.55.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert country name, filing date, and foreign application number in brackets as directed. Use appropriate follow-up to request certified copies.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 2.26 Claimed Foreign Priority - Certified Copy Filed
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledges claim for foreign priority based on an application filed in [1] on [2], but the subsequent nonprovisional or international application designating the U.S. was filed more than 12 months thereafter and no petition under 37 CFR 1.55 or PCT Rule 26bis.3 to restore priority has been granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains petitioner may file 37 CFR 1.55(c) petition to restore if subsequent application filed within two months of expiration and delay unintentional; outlines petition contents: priority claim in ADS, petition fee 1.17(m), statement of unintentional delay; indicate bracket fields for country and filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 2.27 Acknowledge Certified Copy of Foreign Priority Paper in Parent
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledgement that the certified copy of the foreign priority application has been filed in the parent application No. [1], filed on [2].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert series code/serial number of parent. Use this when certified copies are already in parent application rather than the instant application.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 2.30 CPA Status Acceptable (for Design Applications)
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for a Continued Prosecution Application (CPA) filed on [1] under 37 CFR 1.53(d) based on parent Application No. [2] is acceptable and a CPA has been established; an action on the CPA follows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use in the first Office action on a CPA to advise applicant that CPA is established; if a utility/plant CPA was treated as an RCE, do not use this paragraph (use 7.42.15). Insert filing date of CPA request and parent application number in brackets.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 2.31 CPA Status Not Acceptable - Request Not on Separate Paper (for Design Applications)
rubrics_metrics.description: Receipt acknowledged of CPA request filed on [1] under 37 CFR 1.53(d) based on Application No. [2]; because the request was not submitted on a separate paper as required, the request is not acceptable and no CPA has been established.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to inform applicant that CPA request in a design application is noncompliant with 37 CFR 1.53(d)(2). Insert date of paper containing request and application number in brackets.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 2.32 Request To Delete a Named Inventor in CPA (for Design Applications)
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledgement of a statement requesting deletion of [1] as a named inventor filed with the CPA on [2]; inventorship has been corrected as requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert filing date of amendment and designation like 'continuation' or 'divisional' and the prior application number as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 2.35 CPA Status Acceptable - Conditional Request (for Design Applications)
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'conditional' request for a CPA filed on [1] under 37 CFR 1.53(d) based on prior Application No. [2] is treated as acceptable and a CPA has been established; a conditional request submitted as a separate paper is treated as unconditional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use where CPA filed with statement requesting deletion of non-inventor name(s). Insert name(s) requested to be deleted and filing date of CPA. Follow Examiner Note instructions about conditional requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 2.33 New Inventor Identified in CPA (for Design Applications)
rubrics_metrics.description: It is noted that [1] was identified as a named inventor in the CPA filed under 37 CFR 1.53(d) on [2], but no request under 37 CFR 1.48 was filed to correct inventorship; any request to add an inventor must be in the form of a 1.48 request, otherwise inventorship remains the same as in the prior application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use where CPA identifies inventor(s) not named in prior application. Insert name(s) and filing date of CPA in brackets. Advises procedural requirement to file 1.48 for adding inventors.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 2.34 Reference in CPA to Prior Application (by Amendment to the Specification; for Design Applications)
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment requesting that the specification be amended to refer to the present CPA as a [2] application of Application No. [3] has not been entered because, under 37 CFR 1.53(d)(7), the CPA request itself is the specific reference required by 35 U.S.C. 120.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to inform applicant an amendment to the first sentence to refer back to prior application is unnecessary and will be denied entry. Insert amendment filing date, relationship (continuation/divisional), and prior application number in brackets.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 28.01 Header for Statement of Reasons for Substantial New Question of Patentability Determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Header indicating 'REASONS FOR SUBSTANTIAL NEW QUESTION OF PATENTABILITY DETERMINATION' to introduce the examiner's statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use as heading for the SNQ determination in supplemental examination/reexamination contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 28.02 Reasons for Finding No Substantial New Question of Patentability
rubrics_metrics.description: [1], as presented in the request, does not raise a substantial new question of patentability because [2].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In bracket 1 insert the name/description of the item of information (patent, publication, affidavit, sales receipt, transcript, or specific pages/discussion). In bracket 2 insert reasons for determination. Use to explain why a submitted item does not raise an SNQ.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 28.03 Reasons for Finding A Substantial New Question of Patentability
rubrics_metrics.description: [1], as presented in the request, raises a substantial new question of patentability affecting patent claim(s) [2] because [3].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bracket 1: identify item of information; bracket 2: list claims affected; bracket 3: provide reasons why SNQ is raised. If SNQ affects only some claims, explain for which claims and why not for others. Use detailed examples and identification guidance as provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 28.04 Reexamination Ordered Pursuant to 35 U.S.C. 257
rubrics_metrics.description: When a supplemental examination certificate indicates one or more items of information raise an SNQ, ex parte reexamination of claim(s) [3] of U.S. Patent No. [4] is ordered pursuant to 35 U.S.C. 257(b) and 37 CFR 1.625(b); ex parte reexamination will be conducted under 37 CFR 1.530–1.570 with enumerated exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert filing date of supplemental exam proceeding and issue date of certificate (brackets 1 and 2), list claims found to have an SNQ (bracket 3), and list patent number (bracket 4). Explain procedural details: no patent owner's statement under 1.530(a)-(c) may be filed in an ex parte reexamination ordered under 35 U.S.C. 257 until after mailing of first Office action on the merits; assign to art unit and identify control number for future correspondence.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 29.10 Reproductions Objected to, Amended Reproductions Do Not Comply With Formal Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The amended reproductions received on [1] are objected to because [2]; objections per 37 CFR 1.1026 and Rule 9 of the Hague Agreement Common Regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use in international design applications to object to amended reproductions failing formal requirements (quality, explanatory text/legends). Insert date received and reason for objection. Follow with form paragraph 15.05.04.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 29.11 Reproductions Objected to, Design Not Fully Disclosed in Reproductions
rubrics_metrics.description: The reproductions are objected to for failing to fully disclose the industrial design because [1]; use where failure does not render the claimed invention non-enabled and/or indefinite under 35 U.S.C. 112 (e.g., minor inconsistencies among views).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If failure renders design non-enabled/indefinite use form paragraph 15.21 or 15.22 instead. Insert explanation in bracket 1 and follow with 15.05.04.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 29.20 Matter Not Forming Part of Design (International Design Application)
rubrics_metrics.description: Matter shown in a reproduction (environmental structure or portions of the 'article') for which protection is not sought may be indicated by statement in the description and/or by dotted/broken lines or coloring in the reproduction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use only in international design applications; refer to 37 CFR 1.1026 and Hague Agreement Administrative Instruction 403.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 29.21 Rejection, 35 U.S.C. 112(b) - Undescribed Broken Lines (International Design Application)
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim is rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112(b) for failing to particularly point out and distinctly claim the invention because reproductions include broken lines not described in the specification, making scope of claimed design indeterminate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If broken lines represent matter for which protection is not sought, applicant may overcome rejection by inserting statement immediately preceding the claim (provided it does not introduce new matter): e.g., 'The broken line showing of [2] is for the purpose of illustrating [3] and forms no part of the claimed design.' Insert figure numbers and structure/type in brackets as directed. Use in international design applications when reproductions include undescribed broken lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 29.22 Description of Broken Lines Added by Examiner's Amendment (International Design Application)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiner's amendment has added a sentence to the specification immediately preceding the claim clarifying the meaning of broken lines: 'The broken line showing of [1] is for the purpose of illustrating [2] and forms no part of the claimed design.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use only in an Examiner's Amendment for international design applications to explain broken lines. Insert name of structure and whether broken lines indicate portions of the 'article' or environmental structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 29.24 Description of Broken Lines as Boundary of Design Added by Examiner's Amendment (International Design Application)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiner's amendment has added a sentence to the specification: 'The [1] broken line(s) define the bounds of the claimed design and form no part thereof.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when broken lines define boundary and were added by Examiner's Amendment. Insert appropriate descriptor (e.g., portions of the 'article' or environmental structure).

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 29.23 Rejection, 35 U.S.C. 112(b) - Undescribed Broken Lines as Boundary of Design (International Design Application)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim rejected for failing to particularly point out and distinctly claim the invention because reproductions include broken lines not described in the specification and the broken lines are presented as boundary lines, making scope indeterminate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If broken lines represent a boundary for which protection is not sought, applicant may insert statement like: 'The [2] broken line(s) define the bounds of the claimed design and form no part of the claimed design.' Insert type of broken line and other specifics in brackets. Use in international design applications; explain in Examiner's Amendment if applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 29.25 Rejection, 35 U.S.C. 112(b) - Unclear Use of Coloring (International Design Application)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112(b) because reproductions include coloring not described in the specification, making the scope of the claimed design indeterminate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If coloring identifies matter for which protection is not sought, applicant may overcome rejection by inserting a statement immediately preceding the claim (provided no new matter): e.g., 'The portion of the design shown in the color [2] is for the purpose of illustrating [3] and forms no part of the claimed design.' Insert figure numbers, color identification, and whether portions are 'article' or environmental structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 29.26 Description of Coloring Added by Examiner's Amendment (International Design Application)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiner's amendment has added the sentence to the specification: 'The portion of the design shown in the color [1] is for the purpose of illustrating [2] and forms no part of the claimed design.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use only in an Examiner's Amendment for international design applications to explain meaning of coloring in reproductions. Insert color and whether portions are 'article' or environmental structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 29.27 Suggestion To Overcome Rejection Under 35 U.S.C. 112(a) and (b) (International Design Application)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant may indicate that protection is not sought for reproductions considered indefinite or nonenabling by amending reproductions to color those portions or convert them to broken lines and by amending the specification to state that those portions form no part of the claimed design, provided such amendments do not introduce new matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use only in international design applications; insert title of the article in bracket 1. Advises conversion of problematic portions to broken lines or coloring and adding appropriate specification statements consistent with 35 U.S.C. 132 and 37 CFR 1.121.
